properties.name: MEASURED for the islands question, 2026-09-29, over three sources (flo2.io's write log, 157 session transcripts on both machines, and the four designs' structure). Real concurrency is one person's parallel subagents, never two people. No lost work from concurrency was found. Islands at the default depth would be large on reflow2's design and would mostly block a session's own subagents. The only hazard class on record is silent last-writer-wins on one node, which a per-node guard answers
properties.statement:
Anthony asked, 2026-09-29, to study how multi-session work has actually gone before deciding the islands question. Three read-only studies were run.

═══ ① WHO WAS CONCURRENT ═══
- **Across people: never.** flo2.io write log, 09-24..09-29: 2,837 writes. 0 designs have writes, or even reads, from two accounts. The one shared design is flo2 (Anthony and Alex), and Alex has made 0 calls to it.
- **Independent sessions on one design, in the same 10-minute window: 12 windows in a month.** Transcripts, 08-26..09-29: 157 transcripts (69 sessions, 88 subagents), 10,877 landed writes. 8 of the windows were on reflow2's design and 4 on StoryFlow, and there were never more than 2 sessions at once.
- **The real concurrency is PARALLEL SUBAGENTS of one session.**
  - StoryFlow, 09-29: 14 writing subagents on ajs77, up to 10 writers in one 10-minute window. At the gateway, at least 2 writers were in flight together in 28 episodes, and write latency rose from 0.25 s to 1.8–3.7 s behind the single write lock.
  - reflow2's design: triage session c282721e ran 16 subagents, up to 6 at once.

═══ ② COLLISIONS AND LOST WORK ═══
- **Same node, different writers:** 670 pairs in all. 0 within 2 min, 8 within 10 min, 37 within 60 min, 448 more than 24 h apart.
- **Every pair within 60 minutes was informed or an append.** Informed means the later writer had read the node, or seen it in a reply, after the earlier write.
- **Uninformed whole-value overwrites: 20**, all 8–51 h apart, on fields meant to be refreshed (checksums, locations, release status).
- **Lost work attributable to concurrency: none found.**
- **The server side agrees:** 0 same-node writes from provably different clients within 10 minutes.
- **The guard is never used.** expected_content_hash was used 0 times on flo2.io, because it exists only on create_node. The 2 stale-hash refusals seen in transcripts were each a session's own stale hash.
- **The exposure is real, though.** On flo2.io:
  - 167 add_*/create_node calls re-wrote an existing id with no precondition, 76 of them within 10 minutes of the previous write.
  - 123 of 224 replace_text calls had no `old` anchor, so they overwrote the whole field.

═══ ③ WHAT ISLANDS WOULD DO ═══
**Size, measured.** A claimed region is propagate_from(seed, depth) plus the seed, at default depth 2, walked both ways.
- **reflow2's design:**
  - Around an edited node: median 178 nodes (3%), p90 675, max 906.
  - Around an edited Artifact: median 634 (10.6%). Release INCLUDES is 64% of all edges and is walked both ways.
  - Another agent's edit lands inside your depth-2 island 23% of the time (4.8% for intent-layer edits, 98% for artifacts), so parallel code fixes would serialize completely.
  - At depth 1 it is about 1%.
- **The other designs:** medians of 6–18 nodes, and 2–7% of edits land inside.

**Simulated on the transcripts** (reflow2, 1 hop, 60 min):
- 150 warnings would fire.
- 137 of them are against the session's OWN subagents.
- 0 coincided with a real overwrite.
- Refusals would have blocked the parallelism actually in use.

**Recorded incidents it would have prevented: none.**
- The same-node lost updates on record are all from August on dev_storyflow's old local fleet: one deliberate race, the 90-second frag:ownership_guard collision, and a stale batch revert by the same worker.
- The one recorded field use of the compare-and-swap refused correctly.
- Every other recorded collision was on shared context OUTSIDE the nodes, and neither islands nor a node guard reach those:
  - one live store serving every branch (12+ times);
  - branch records in the live store (09-22, repeated 09-29);
  - a shared cargo target dir, where the fix chosen was an exclusive lock because the corruption was silent;
  - git stash;
  - bus files.

═══ ④ PREREQUISITES ANY OPTION HITS ═══
- **Identity:** fact:a-claim-cannot-tell-two-agents-of-one-person-apart-and-on-flo2-io-not-even-two-people-2026-09-29.
- **Liveness:** the 300 s seat flip is still in the code.
- **Option (d) needs a token on the read path.** Reads carry no content hash today: get_node, scan_nodes and search hits have none. Its scope is 8 constructors (plus create_nodes) for the common edits, and about 60 write tools for "any second edit to one node". One `_meta` precondition checked inside write_lock could replace most per-tool parameters.

═══ WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE OPTIONS (a finding, not a decision) ═══
- **(a) and (b), refusal inside a region:** not supported by the data. They would stall the owner's own subagents, prevent nothing on record, and cannot be built soundly until identity and liveness are fixed.
- **(d), a per-node guard:** answers the one hazard class on record and needs no identity.
- **(c), a warning:** useful only once each agent has its own identity, and quiet only at depth 1 or with a traversal that drops release packaging.

Limits:
- Transcripts older than about 30 days are pruned.
- claude.ai web and mobile writers are invisible to the transcript study.
- flo2.io's minted-seat liveness comes from reading the code, not from a test.
- The overlap probabilities assume independent seeds.
